# Session 3 — case manager, discharge planning (synthetic)

Interviewer: Where does discharge planning start for you?
Amara Okafor: Day one of admission, ideally. In practice I find out a patient is "ready" when the charge nurse flags me in the hallway. The system has a discharge milestone checklist but nobody fills it in real time — it gets backfilled at the end.
Interviewer: Why does it get backfilled?
Amara Okafor: Because filling it means logging into a shared workstation, badge-tap, two-factor, then six clicks to the right tab. On a unit where you're interrupted every ninety seconds, that's fantasy. I batch it at my desk after rounds.
Interviewer: What breaks because of that?
Amara Okafor: Transport shows up for a patient whose ride home isn't arranged. Pharmacy hasn't done med reconciliation because their trigger is the checklist I haven't filled. The patient sits dressed on the bed for four hours. Families call me directly now — they've learned the system doesn't tell them anything.
Interviewer: One fix?
Amara Okafor: Let me update milestones from my phone in the hallway, two taps. And make the checklist drive everyone else's queues for real, because right now it's decoration.
